rail_guard.text: Great Victoria Street. Trains to every station on this island you've visited. Please mind the gap, the step, and the seagull on the bench.
Hop aboard. The Wildlore rail runs to any town you have visited on this island. Where to?

then.text: Cairnryan, is it? The Selkie sails when the tide's right and the tea's brewed. Mind the gulls. They're organised.

else.text: Ah, the Selkie's not sailing for you yet, love. Scotland's a long way to go with an unfinished to-do list.
Go and see Keeper Ruairí at the shipyard first. Past the cranes, the big shed with the sparks. He's friendly. Mostly to people who've just lost to him, but still.

titanic_guide.text: Welcome to Titanic Belfast! Harland and Wolff built the ship here, and it sailed in 1912. The story's sad, but the building is a joy, and the gift shop has a very good fudge.
Did you know the Titanic had a sister ship, the Olympic, built right alongside her? The Olympic sailed for 24 years. Nobody tells you that, because it's a lovely story with no iceberg.

dock_worker.text: I look up at Samson and Goliath every day. Hundred metres of yellow steel. They're no longer needed to build ships, but they're loved. We would never take them down.
On a Friday, the whole city looks up at them and says, 'right, that's us'. It's a Belfast thing.

black_taxi.text: City tour? I'll take you round all of it, the shipyard, the Cathedral Quarter, the lot, and I'll tell you every story twice, once with feeling.
Belfast's got a sense of humour like nobody else's. It's the only city I know where 'not bad' is a standing ovation.

park_busker.text: Fiddle, whistle, and a bodhran on my knee. I'm a one-man session. If the rain comes, I'll be a one-man wet session.
'Craic' is the word for fun and gossip. If you've had good craic, you've had a good time. If you've had bad craic, you've been in a meeting.

bridge_walker.text: The Lagan used to be so muddy you'd never guess there was a river. Now it's full of life: seals, salmon, even a few brave kayakers.
There's a huge fish sculpture down by the Waterfront, covered in tiles telling the history of Belfast. It's been called the Big Fish for twenty years. Nobody has come up with a better name.

gate_belfast_north.text: Road's closed. Works on the Antrim coast. Very serious works. We've a cone.
The Keeper at the shipyard has the say on this road, and he hasn't said it yet. Ask Ruairí. Past the cranes, the big shed. You can't miss the sparks.
